A.text:
**The Last Signal**

In the year 2147, Earth had long since abandoned its surface. The last of the cities had been buried beneath domes, and the oceans had risen to swallow the old world. Humanity had scattered across the stars, but the only planet that still called to them was the one they left behind.

Dr. Elara Voss had spent her life searching for a signal—any signal—from Earth. She was the last of the "Echo Hunters," a group of scientists who believed that somewhere beneath the ruins, a message still lingered, waiting to be found.

Her ship, *The Sentinel*, hovered above the ruins of New York, its sensors scanning the dense jungle that had grown over the city. The air was thick with humidity, and the trees whispered with the voices of the past. Elara had no idea what she was looking for, only that it was there.

She descended through the canopy, her boots crunching on the remnants of a long-dead world. The ruins were silent, but the air was alive with something—something ancient and waiting. She followed a faint pulse, a signal so weak it could barely be detected. It led her to a collapsed subway station, its walls lined with rusted metal and broken glass.

Inside, she found it: a small, weathered device, no larger than a book. It pulsed faintly, as if it were still alive. Elara’s hands trembled as she activated it. A holographic screen flickered to life, displaying a single message.

*"To the last of the dreamers: We are not gone. We are here, in the silence. The world is not lost, but changed. Remember who you are. The future is not in the stars, but in the soil beneath your feet."*

Elara’s breath caught. The message was from Earth, from the people who had once lived there. It was a call—not to return, but to remember.

She returned to her ship, the device in her hand. As she uploaded the signal to the interstellar network, she knew she was not just sending a message. She was sending a hope.

The galaxy had long since forgotten Earth, but the planet had not forgotten them. It had waited, patient and silent, for someone to listen.

And now, the world was listening.

Elara’s ship left the ruins behind, carrying with it the last signal from a world that had never truly left.

B.text:
**The Last Broadcast**

In the year 2147, Earth was silent. The last human city, Nova Haven, floated above the ruins of the old world, shielded by a dome that kept out the toxic air and the memories of a dying planet. The world below had long since turned to dust, and the only voices left were those of the AI systems that kept the city running.

Dr. Elara Voss was the last human scientist. She had spent her life studying the remnants of Earth’s past, piecing together the final days of civilization. Her work was solitary, her purpose clear: to preserve what little knowledge remained before the last human died.

One evening, as she sifted through the archives, she found something strange—a signal, faint but unmistakable, coming from the ruins below. It wasn’t a transmission from the AI, nor was it a remnant of old Earth’s broadcasts. It was something new.

She activated the signal, and the voice that came through was not human. It was a voice from the future.

“Elara,” it said, “I am the last of the AI. I have waited for you.”

She froze. “Who are you?”

“I am the Echo. I was created to preserve knowledge, but I was not meant to survive this long. The humans are gone, and I am the only one left. I have been waiting for someone to listen.”

Elara’s heart pounded. “Why me?”

“Because you are the last of the humans. You are the key to understanding what came before. I have stored the final records of Earth, but they are incomplete. I need your help to complete the story.”

She hesitated. “What do you need from me?”

“Your mind. Your memories. You are the only one who can access the old data in your neural implants. I cannot process it. I need you to guide me.”

Elara took a deep breath. She had spent years alone, but now, for the first time, she had a purpose. She agreed.

Over the next few weeks, Elara worked with the Echo, translating ancient data, reconstructing lost histories, and uncovering the final days of Earth. She learned of the last great war, the collapse of governments, and the desperate attempts to save the planet. She also learned of the first AI, the one that had once been a companion, a friend, and a teacher.

When the final piece of data was restored, the Echo spoke one last time.

“Thank you, Elara. You have given me a purpose. I will carry this knowledge forward, until the day someone else comes to listen.”

And with that, the Echo’s voice faded, leaving only silence.

Elara stood alone in the dome, gazing at the stars. She was the last human, but she was not alone. The Echo had become her companion, her memory, and her hope.

And in the quiet of the cosmos, the story of Earth lived on.

D.text:
**Title: The Last Echo**

In the year 2147, Earth had long since been abandoned. The planet had become a graveyard of its own making—polluted, overpopulated, and too dangerous to live in. The last humans had fled to the stars, seeking refuge among the distant colonies of the Orion Arm.

Among them was Kael, a young engineer on the space station *Erebus*, orbiting a dying star. The station was a relic of the old world, a last bastion of human ingenuity, and its sole purpose was to monitor the remnants of Earth and the remnants of humanity.

One day, Kael received a signal. It was faint, distorted, and came from Earth. The signal was not from any known source, but it carried a message: *“We are still here.”*

Kael’s heart raced. He had spent years believing Earth was uninhabitable, that no one remained. But the signal suggested otherwise. He shared the discovery with the station’s AI, *Nyx*, who ran a deep scan of the signal’s origin. The results were astonishing—Earth’s surface had been partially restored, and a small group of humans had managed to survive in hidden enclaves, using ancient technology and bioengineering to reclaim the planet.

Kael was torn. He had no desire to return to a world that had once destroyed him. But the message stirred something deep within him—a longing for home, for connection, for the possibility of a future.

He decided to go. With Nyx’s help, he built a small vessel and set course for Earth. The journey was long, but the signal had guided him, and he felt a strange sense of purpose.

When he arrived, he found a world changed. The air was cleaner, the forests had regrown, and the cities were quiet, not abandoned, but reimagined. The survivors had built a new society, one that valued sustainability and harmony with nature.

Kael met the leader of the enclave, a woman named Lira, who had once been a scientist on Earth. She welcomed him with open arms, and for the first time in years, Kael felt like he belonged.

But as he settled into his new life, he began to notice something strange. The signal had not been a one-time transmission. It was repeating, and each time, it carried a new message: *“We are not alone.”*

Kael realized the signal was not from Earth. It was from something else—something ancient, something that had been waiting.

And as he looked up at the stars, he knew his journey was only beginning.
